plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with small yellow flowers (cyathia) surrounded by showy colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals. In frost-free climates it grows into a large landscape shrub up to 3 meters tall, and as a potted plant it is a symbol of the holiday season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown as an outdoor shrub in warm regions such as California, Florida, Hawaii and the Mediterranean, and as a houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: The colored parts are modified leaves called bracts, whose color change is triggered by long nights. The Aztecs called the plant cuetlaxochitl and used it to make a reddish dye.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with flattened, segmented stems with pointed teeth along the edges. Arching branch tips bear tubular, zygomorphic flowers in profusion. In the wild it grows on tree branches and in rock crevices in humid forests.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November to January) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil near Rio de Janeiro; widely grown as a houseplant globally
plants.funFact: It blooms in response to short days and cool nights. Unlike desert cacti, it grows in the shade of Brazilian rainforest trees and prefers humidity.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading, umbrella-shaped tree with fern-like feathery leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere's early summer it is covered in clusters of large, bright flowers, and it later produces long woody seed pods.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January); also blooms at other times in the tropics, mostly in the dry season
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; planted in tropical and subtropical regions including Australia, South Africa, Brazil, India and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: Although it is a famous ornamental tree across the tropics, it is endangered in its native Madagascar, where its dry forest habitat has been greatly reduced.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, often lightly fragrant flowers with a boss of yellow stamens. It blooms earlier than the common camellia and tolerates more sun, making it popular for hedges and espaliers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (October to January)
plants.location: Native to Japan (southern islands) and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe's mild regions, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Sasanqua is a source of tea seed oil, which is used in cooking, cosmetics and hair care in Japan. The related Camellia sinensis is the plant used to make tea.
